$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Cosmos DB (SQL / Core API). See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.cosmos.account.crud.title: Database accounts (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.cosmos.data_explorer.title: Data Explorer: databases, containers and documents over the native Cosmos DB REST (SQL/Core API) data plane
limitations: The Cosmos data-plane store is a single keyspace shared by every Cosmos account in this Vyomi environment (no per-account partitioning) — a database id created under one account is visible from any other account's Data Explorer.

New Container accepts a hierarchical partition key request, a unique key policy and analytical store enablement the way the real form submits them, but only the indexing policy (on/off) round-trips for real; the others are accepted and not enforced.

azure.cosmos.query.title: SQL query (SELECT) over the Cosmos data plane
limitations: Covers a pragmatic SELECT subset (projection, a single WHERE comparison/IN predicate, ORDER BY); joins, subqueries, aggregate/system functions and stored procedures are not implemented.

azure.cosmos.default_consistency.title: Default consistency level
limitations: properties.consistencyPolicy.defaultConsistencyLevel round-trips through ARM, but every data-plane read in Vyomi is already strongly consistent regardless of the configured level.

azure.cosmos.replicate_data_globally.title: Replicate data globally (region list, failover)
limitations: properties.locations round-trips through ARM, but Vyomi has one logical region: added regions are not separately provisioned, and Manual/Service-Managed Failover do not move the data plane anywhere.

azure.cosmos.backup_restore.title: Backup & Restore policy
limitations: properties.backupPolicy round-trips through ARM exactly as configured at create time, but Vyomi never takes or restores a backup.

azure.cosmos.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the database account
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this account); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.cosmos.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered ARM mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.cosmos.iam.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), but the generic ARM list is subscription-wide (not scoped to this one account), and 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation is not modelled — Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment.
